lead_headline: Chick-fil-A debuts Colorado's first drive-thru-only location at Central Park as 8 new leads surface

restaurant.blurb: 8 new leads today: Red Lotus Den food hall (Westminster, June target), DiFranco's Italian (Westminster second location), Chick-fil-A drive-thru-only (Central Park, opened today), Wash Park Social (replaces Grille).

foreclosure.blurb: $6.1M Douglas County filing at 18901 Longs Way — the week's only filing exceeding $4M threshold, followed by a $2.9M Arapahoe County property at 5899 Green Oaks Dr.

liquor.blurb: 6 new applications today — headlined by The Denver Book Society (Humboldt Street hotel/restaurant license), Skyline Beer Garden (Arapahoe Street combined liquor transfer), and Pan Gu Asian Bistro (Aurora). Four status changes overnight: Denver Hot Pot cleared delinquency to active, while Molotov (Colfax), Hungry Elephant (Cherry Creek), and Rootdown DIA all slipped to delinquent. The 7-day count hits 22 applications — 5.5× last week's anemic 4-application tally and the strongest weekly filing surge since late winter.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention today pushes the 7-day total to 52 across 17 sources — matching last week's 51-mention baseline after April's early surge. Instagram (11), Denver Post (10), and X (6) dominate this week's pickups. Standout coverage: Post's 56-restaurant tipped wage letter, Facebook amplification of Flats groundbreaking and fastest-growing companies retrospective, Reddit's Littleton restaurant subsidy debate. The week-over-week plateau suggests April's opening frenzy has normalized into steady-state spring coverage after three weeks of elevated activity.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +0 yesterday (0 new, 0 canceled) marks the fourth consecutive flat day and holds MTD at +10 (+0.6/day), 90-day net at +138. The current four-day drought (April 13-16) follows April 7-12's exceptional six-day run (+11 net, 15 new vs 4 canceled) — the strongest sustained performance since late March. Week-over-week momentum has cooled sharply: this week's +5 net (7 new, 2 canceled) trails last week's +12 by 58%, though cancellation rate improved dramatically (2 vs 8). The MTD +0.6/day pace lags YTD's +1.3/day average, but mid-month weekday flatlines typically precede month-end renewal clusters.
